To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The equilibrium density, rate of approach to it, and the equilibrium values are all strongly dependent on the detuning of the forcing frequency from the resonant frequency of the Duffing oscillator.

the equilibrium phase space density is a function of the forcing amplitude and the detuning parameter and the equilibrium density is a function only of the detuning parameter in the linear regime of forcing, that the equilibrium density is independent of the forcing amplitude in the non-linear regime and that the rate of approach towards the equilibrium density is faster in the non-linear and the intermediate regimes.

the equilibrium density, the equilibrium emittance growth rate and the time required to approach equilibrium depend crucially on detuning and that there are three distinct regimes of forcing, characterized by different detuning values, that lead to the largest equilibrium emittance growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of a large number of coupled Duffing oscillating systems with forcing.
the collective dynamics of a large number of forced Duffings oscillators.
the collective dynamics of a system of Duffing oscillations, which are coupled through the power supply ripple.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dipole ripple emittance growth is dominated by the forcing amplitude in a low frequency regime and by the detuning in two high frequency regimes, and that the detuning is the dominant effect in the intermediate regime.
the emittance growth due power supply ripple in dipole magnets can be modeled by forced duffing oscillations with an appropriate choice of the detuning and forcing amplitude.
, for a given amplitude, the maximum emittance growth occurs at a frequency which is a function of the detuning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emittance growth is maximum for a detuning parameter of the order of the damping parameter and the forcing amplitude has a threshold value below which no emittance growth is observed.
the emittance growth is largest when the forcing frequency is close to the natural frequency of the Duffing oscillator.
the emittance growth due the power supply ripple is a non-linear phenomenon which is sensitive to the forcing amplitude, forcing frequency and the phase of the power supply ripple.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emittance growth due the dipole ripple can be significantly reduced by a proper choice of the detuning parameter and the forcing amplitude.
the emittance growth is largest when the detuning parameter is close to a value where the equilibrium density is a delta function.
the emittance growth due power supply ripple in the dipoles can be reduced by operating the storage ring with a detuning parameter which minimizes the equilibrium value of the emittance.
